client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: Which intervention is appropriate as part of a hospitalized client’s fall-prevention plan when the client is not receiving direct bedside care?

options.A: Keep the bed in a low position with the wheels locked according to the individualized plan.
options.B: Raise the bed to its highest position so the client can stand more quickly.
options.C: Leave the bed wheels unlocked so the bed can move if the client loses balance.
options.D: Place frequently used items on the floor beside the bed.

rationale: AHRQ fall-prevention resources include maintaining a safe environment with the bed in an appropriate low position and wheels locked as part of fall-risk reduction. Fall interventions should be individualized to the patient.
educational_objective: Apply safe bed positioning as part of fall prevention.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
source_document_title: Preventing Falls in Hospitals / Fall Prevention Best Practices
source_locator: Hospital fall-prevention best practices—safe environment; bed position and wheel locking
source_claim_supported: Low/appropriate bed positioning with locked wheels is a recognized hospital fall-prevention measure.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Corrected blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety and removed the unsupported claim that the primary purpose is specifically to reduce fall distance.
audit_findings: Correct option is a recognized fall-safety measure.
Independent second pass found a unique answer.
